source.title: From Isolation to Entanglement: When Do Interpretability Methods Identify and Disentangle Known Concepts?
source.authors: Aaron Mueller; Andrew Lee; Shruti B. Joshi; E. Lubana; Dhanya Sridhar; P. Reizinger

record.tranche_reason: The study measures how well dimensions of the models’ native activation representations disentangle known concepts using DCI-ES, a different measure from the original neuron examples. It reports that native representations are less disentangled than SAE features.
record.gate_note: The raw-neuron evidence relevant to the claim is the DCI-ES disentanglement result for the identity-featurized native representation. Most steering results concern SAE features, not neurons, and are not recorded as neuron findings. The paper also cites results from other work; those are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is an evaluation of SAE and probe featurizers on four PCFG-labelled concepts. Its 'Neuron' condition is the raw middle-layer output h_ℓ, an identity-featurizer baseline. The appendix calls it the 'residual neuron baseline', so it is residual-stream dimensions, not MLP neurons. It is scored with DCI-ES against four known concepts and reported only as a comparison point for the authors' featurizers. No rate or share of neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts is given, and no layer comparison is made. The study builds on the premise that activation dimensions are polysemantic but does not test it.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly right. The authors find that SAEs and probes score high on correlational disentanglement (D, I, E) but low on completeness, i.e. concepts are split across features. They report improvements over the native neuron-based space. Steering one top feature nonetheless often affects other concepts, despite near-perfect disjointness (no interaction effects). They conclude that correlational metrics do not predict steering selectivity, and that multi-concept, interventional evaluations are needed.
record.recipe_differences: Uses PCFG-generated language data with known concept labels, DCI-ES/MCC evaluations, and feature steering; it does not reproduce the cited vision-neuron or SoLU methods.
record.method_sensitivity: The representation type (native activation dimensions versus SAE architectures) changes reported disentanglement. The study also varies cross-concept correlation, but the text does not report a specific native-neuron DCI trend for those settings.

fits_no_version.finding: Raw middle-layer residual-stream dimensions of Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B score lower DCI disentanglement on four synthetic concepts than SAE features. The text says D is high for SAEs 'but not for the original representation space'. Exact values appear only in the Figure 3 plot. k-sparse probes on the residual stream need more dimensions to reach peak MCC.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Native residual-stream dimensions of language models mix known concepts more than SAE features do, by DCI-ES disentanglement.

record.peer_reviewed: Annual Meeting of the Association for Computational Linguistics
record.problems: The neuron-related result is a DCI-ES aggregate on synthetic data, not a count of individual polysemantic neurons or an analysis of unrelated natural tokens and contexts. Figure 3 does not give exact native-representation DCI values in the text. The study uses four categorical concepts and reports only middle-layer representations for this comparison.
record.rows_left_out: Steering and selectivity results for SAE features, probe results, and SAE architecture comparisons were left out because they do not measure native neuron polysemanticity. No other neuron-relevant native-representation DCI results were reported beyond Figure 3.

untested.parts: No MLP neurons are examined. There is no share of neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts, and no comparison across layers.
Superposition is not tested as a cause.
Initialization, regularization and training noise are not tested as causes.
Model activation functions and architectures are not varied. Only featurizers are compared.
Activation range and explanation scoring are not varied for neurons.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's V2 links and labels are dropped. The 'Neuron' condition is the residual-stream output (h_ℓ at the middle layer), not MLP neurons. It is a baseline for the paper's featurizer comparison, and DCI over four labelled concepts is not a measure of neurons responding to unrelated inputs.

versions.untested_parts: Vision classifiers and the InceptionV1 neuron example are not studied.

The study evaluates native activation dimensions on four labeled concepts in synthetic PCFG-generated sentences, not the share of MLP neurons responding to unrelated tokens or contexts across language-model layers.
The study does not test superposition or whether feature capacity pressure causes polysemantic neurons.
The study does not test whether initialization, regularization, or training noise causes polysemantic neurons when capacity is sufficient.

It compares featurizer types, but does not test changes in the share of polysemantic neurons across model activation functions or architectures, or establish a performance-cost result for reducing that share.
The study does not investigate whether canonical polysemantic neurons detect a shared feature or related offshoots of one job.
The study does not vary activation range or explanation-scoring rules to estimate how those choices change neuron polysemanticity.

rows.subject: Pythia-70M
rows.operation_detail: Measured DCI-ES disentanglement for the native activation representation, equivalent to an identity featurizer.
rows.measure: DCI-ES disentanglement of native activation dimensions with respect to the four labeled concepts
rows.uncertainty: 1 std. dev. across 3 training seeds (shaded regions)
rows.note: The text says DCI disentanglement is high for SAE architectures but not for the original representation space, and describes SAE disentanglement as improved over the native neuron-based representation. The plot does not provide an exact value or the fraction of dimensions that are mixed.
rows.check: Subject is Pythia-70M residual-stream output at layer 3, not MLP neurons. The measure is DCI disentanglement over four concepts, not polysemanticity toward unrelated inputs. The row is a baseline compared against the study's own featurizers. The value is figure-only.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.condition: Native activation representations of Pythia-70M and Gemma-2-2B on the generated four-concept language task
reader_labels.reason: The native-representation DCI disentanglement is described as poorer than SAE disentanglement, consistent with dimensions mixing concepts; see V2-PY-D-rho0.0 through V2-PY-D-rho1.0 and V2-GEM-D-rho0.0 through V2-GEM-D-rho1.0.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: It reports no proportion of mixed neurons and evaluates four known concepts in synthetic sentences at a middle layer, rather than neuron responses to unrelated tokens or contexts across layers; see the same DCI rows.
